newsitem.title: USA: U.S. anti-drug czar defends Mexico decision.
newsitem.headline: U.S. anti-drug czar defends Mexico decision.

text.p: The top U.S. anti-drug official Gen. Barry McCaffrey said on Sunday critics of the U.S. decision to certify Mexico as an ally in the drug war may be guilty of "creative hypocrisy."

McCaffrey said there is drug-related violence and corruption on both sides of the Mexican border and that to an extent the $6 billion in drug-related money pouring out of the United States is responsible for an "international crime wave.

"There is an element of creative hypocrisy to focusing on Mexico which stands between us and a source of cocaine. So our money is fuelling in many ways an international crime wave," the director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy McCaffrey said on ABC's "This Week.
In the most recent Mexican drug scandal, suspected drug launderer Humberto Garcio Abrego was released inexplicably from police custody hours before Clinton's decision on Mexico.
"I don't want to talk about the details because I think the story is going to get worse before it gets better," McCaffrey said.
He said U.S. officials had opted for partnership with Mexico "while pushing for concrete results."
"I suggest to people, if you want to fight a war on drugs, sit down at your own kitchen table and talk to your own children," he said.
He said Colombia, which was not certified, is different, partly because coca and opium production rose last year and because drug money's corrupting influence has been pervasive.
"Many of us believe that President (Ernesto) Samper and the senior officers of government are fundamentally contaminated by this drug corruption," he said.
